A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RO-HNN research, with matching authors, methods and three simulated systems. All 28 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original pendulum, particle-vortex and cloth simulations, prediction errors, architectural ablations and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix H.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, noise and sample-size studies, component ablations and runtime analyses in Section 4 and Appendices I–J.

M1.justification: The cotangent-lifted symplectic autoencoder, geometric Hamiltonian network, SPD mass/damping parametrizations, Strang integration and joint multi-step loss remain. Expanded implementation explanations and the dissipative-system proposition describe or justify the existing procedure; the added architectures serve as comparisons and ablations.

E1.justification: The same 15-DoF pendulum, 90-DoF vortex and 600-DoF cloth remain. V2 adds a limited observation-corruption scenario: training on pendulum observations with Gaussian noise at 5% and 10% scales, followed by evaluation on clean trajectories (Appendix I.1).

E2.justification: V2 adds HNKO comparisons on all three systems and geometric and black-box RO-LNN comparisons on cloth. It also adds nonsymplectic-AE variants for vortex and cloth, a black-box HNN cloth comparison, and analytic-FOM and AE-implementation timing comparators. The earlier SMG, weakly symplectic AE and HNN comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols cover noise-corrupted training, full-model training with 1,000/3,000/6,000 samples, additional comparator architectures and budgets, and solver-step-size/runtime comparisons. V2 Appendix H.2.2 also corrects the reported vortex latent dimensions from 3/6 to 6/10 and AE widths from 32/64/128/600 to 32/48/64/90 relative to v1 Appendix G.2.2. These reported corrections do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds noise robustness, full RO-HNN sample-size sensitivity, learned pendulum latent-trajectory inspection, and nonsymplectic-AE ablations. The cloth study newly crosses AE structure with Strang versus Runge–Kutta integration (Figure 20), while Appendix J analyzes accuracy–runtime tradeoffs and analytical versus autodifferentiated lifts. V1's latent-HNN data-doubling, latent-dimension, joint-training and damping ablations are retained.

E5.justification: V1 already reports means and standard deviations over test trajectories. V2 Table 7 newly reports a sample-size study involving ten models trained from different random seeds, and Figure 2 adds explicitly identified median/quartile bands. This expands uncertainty reporting locally without establishing increased seed counts for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: Shared numerical entries in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged, and v1's runtime Table 5 reappears unchanged as v2 Table 9. Substantial new results include HNKO's 5-second pendulum position error of 1.32 ± 0.94, sample-size-dependent RO-HNN losses in Table 7, and cloth runtimes of 16.01 seconds for RO-HNN versus 255.24 seconds for the FOM under the listed fine-step Strang settings (Table 8). These are additional comparisons, not performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 3.3/D.3 and a proof concerning preservation of forced, Rayleigh-damped structure under reduction, including derivation of the positive-semidefinite reduced damping matrix. The original projection and symplecticity proofs are retained in Appendix D. The new damping-force derivation nevertheless uses a positive force contribution where Equation 11 subtracts damping, leaving a sign inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same three contributions: the constrained symplectic AE, geometric HNN and jointly trained RO-HNN. The central claims of physically consistent, stable, generalizable prediction of high-dimensional dynamics remain; the added experiments provide broader support without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes nonsymplectic dissipative flow from preservation of the reduced force-field structure and discusses port/contact-Hamiltonian connections. It adds hypotheses explaining nonsymplectic-AE effects, RO-HNN versus RO-LNN accuracy, and Strang integration's performance under dissipation. The latent-dimension tradeoff emphasized in the conclusion was already discussed in v1 Appendix H.2.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a source-code link, detailed analytical cotangent-lift derivatives and intermediate-state handling, implementation/training specifications for the new baselines, and runtime hardware and measurement details. V1 already states that it uses analytical layerwise differentiation; the expanded Appendix E documents that implementation rather than establishing a new computational procedure. The linked resource's availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning to Hamiltonian graph networks and Koopman approaches, adding discussion of their assumptions and differences from reduced nonlinear dynamics. It also adds Poisson-system references and literature supporting the HNN/LNN interpretation, while retaining the original MOR lineage. The PINN discussion replaces Karniadakis et al. with Saqlain et al.; bibliographic updates to retained works are separate from these additions.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the original wording remain. Focused revisions expand the introduction, dissipative-model explanation and conclusion, move the original proofs into Appendix D, consolidate runtimes in Appendix J, and add a terminology guide and Impact Statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with extensive resizing and relocation. Tables 1, 3 and 4 expand; cloth panels from v1 Figure 11 move into the expanded v2 Figure 5. New displays cover notation, noise, sample size, component ablations and runtimes, while some new boxplots redisplay existing comparisons.

improvement.justification: V2 closes important validation gaps through Koopman/Lagrangian comparisons, noise and ten-seed sample-size studies, dissipative-component controls, and accuracy/runtime analyses. These substantially strengthen support for the geometry and scalability claims, while added implementation details improve reproducibility. The sign inconsistency in the new damping derivation limits the theoretical clarification, but does not outweigh the broader empirical and documentation gains.
